Subtract $\frac{\pi}{4}$ from each asymptote of $y=\arctan x$.
$y=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{4}$
$y=-\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}=-\frac{3\pi}{4}$

Reflecting in the $x$-axis multiplies the function by $-1$.
$y=-\arcsin x$
Translating $\frac{\pi}{2}$ units up adds $\frac{\pi}{2}$ to the function.
$y=-\arcsin x+\frac{\pi}{2}$

questions.solution_text:
The asymptotes of $y=a\arctan x+c$ are $y=\frac{a\pi}{2}+c$ and $y=-\frac{a\pi}{2}+c$.
Adding the two given values gives $2c=2+(-4)$
$c=-1$
Subtracting gives $a\pi=2-(-4)$
$a\pi=6$
$a=\frac{6}{\pi}$
